thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN — sev2: serving-runtime GPU node flapping detected (gpu-12). auto-alert at 2026-03-15T09:12:01Z. tagging oncall.
emma-oncall: taking lead. seeing repeated 'CUDA illegal memory access' in runtime logs, plus container restarts ~1m apart.
raj-eng: can you paste the tail of the runtime logs? I want kernel trace + OOM lines.
emma-oncall: pasting snippets below.
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] runtime: ERROR cuda: illegal memory access at kernel.cu:412
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] runtime: stack: launch_kernel -> copy_kv_cache -> forward_step
[2026-03-15T09:12:00Z] kubelet: Container crashed: exit_code=139 signal=11
[2026-03-15T09:12:24Z] runtime: OOM when allocating 512MB workspace
```
carla-support: any customer-facing impact yet? which deployments hit?
emma-oncall: early read: two jobs on gpu-12 (prod/decoder-v2 and prod/embeddings) had errors. traffic rerouted by router fallback to cpu-pool, so high latency for a subset of requests (~2-3s extra). No errors seen on dedicated pools.
sara-infra: I just saw kube events: node gpu-12 kernel logs showing 'unaligned address fault' and then SMMU errors. I'm pulling dmesg.
dinesh-ml: could be a kernel/driver race with our new fused-kernel launch path. We enabled continuous-batching kernel 2 days ago for this model cohort. Might be related to "async-kernel-warm" opt.
raj-eng: prioritize containment: 1) cordon gpu-12, 2) drain noncritical pods, 3) route incoming inference for those model routes to fallback variants. I'll start drain but keep a small canary of decoder-v2 on node to repro.
ops-bot: command run: `kubectl cordon gpu-12` by sara-infra at 2026-03-15T09:14:05Z
ops-bot: command run: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` by sara-infra at 2026-03-15T09:14:24Z
emma-oncall: note: don't evict long-lived dedicated jobs; use label selector to only drain hosted inference pods.
raj-eng: rolling back the continuous-batching kernel flag to previous safe value for decoder-v2 in the runtime config. pushing a small config change to canary (one pod).
dinesh-ml: good — also enable verbose CUDA checks (NV_CHECK=1) on canary to collect PTX traces. We'll need to confirm whether this is driver bug vs model kernel.
carla-support: drafting customer blurb: "We've detected intermittent GPU node failures causing elevated latency for a subset of requests. Traffic has been routed to fallback compute while we mitigate. We'll update in 30m." ok?
emma-oncall: SGTM. include affected model names + approximate percent of traffic (0.7% of total requests).
sara-infra: dmesg snippet:
```
[Mar15 09:11:57] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, PID=2145, 0x00000000
[Mar15 09:11:58] kernel: vm_fault: unaligned address 0x7fff9abc1234 in mm_struct 0x7f8a...
[Mar15 09:12:01] smmu: page table walk failed for device 0000:03:00.0
```
raj-eng: those Xid 31 + SMMU failures point to a device address translation hiccup. Could be a driver/hardware firmware mismatch triggered by our new kernel path.
dinesh-ml: we should collect a CUDA nsight/pttrace but that requires reproducer. I'll coordinate offline. For now, recommend: pin model to cpu-fallback for user-facing hosts and restart runtime process on a fresh GPU node with older driver.

- (sara) keep node cordoned + mark for manual reboot and driver rollback if repro confirmed
- (raj) push runtime config rollback & enable verbose checks on canary
- (dinesh) gather traces from canary; attempt repro on isolated harness
- (carla) customer comms + incident page update
- (kai) next oncall for 09:40UTC handoff
